title: 29 men vanished in 30 seconds. What really sank the Edmund Fitzgerald?
description:
On November 10, 1975, the SS Edmund Fitzgerald vanished from radar during a brutal storm on Lake Superior. The 729-foot freighter, loaded with 26,000 tons of iron ore, went down with 29 men and no distress call.

Captain McSorley radioed that they were "holding our own" just ten minutes before the ship disappeared. While the Coast Guard blamed failed hatch covers, evidence suggests she may have silently scraped a shallow shoal, leading to catastrophic flooding.

The wreck was found split in two 530 feet below the surface. The exact cause remains disputed, and the men's bodies were never recovered due to the lake's freezing depths. Subscribe now 👇
